title: incus VM definition
description: One incus VM, provisioned from the HOST via `incus exec` (no ansible/python inside the guest). Field contract: ../SPEC.md.

template_name.description: Template id - the `<template_name>` you pass to `ivm init <template_name>`. NOT the VM instance name: the instance name is chosen interactively at init (default `<template_name>-<cwd-path>`, editable) and bound to the dir via the VM's `user.ivm_host_bound_dir` config (`user.ivm_init_at_dir` just records where init ran).

description.description: One-line human summary of this template, shown by `ivm init` run with no template arg (the listing). Optional.

host_bound_dir.description: REQUIRED. The HOST dir this VM is bound to for cwd resolution, written to the VM's `user.ivm_host_bound_dir` tag at init (`user.ivm_init_at_dir` separately records where init ran, as pure history). Shell-expanded on the HOST like a mount's `host` value: `$(pwd)` = bind to the dir `ivm init` runs in (the project-box default, e.g. claude/codex); a relative result is made absolute against that dir. The literal `__HOST_CWD_IS_NOT_BOUND__` = deliberately unbound (appliance templates, e.g. llm_*): the VM never resolves by cwd - target it by name (`ivm shell <vm>` / `--name <vm>`; `ivm cd` refuses it) - and the default instance name drops the path suffix (`ivm-<template_name>`). Re-bind/unbind later with `ivm set`/`unset host-bound-dir`.

hw.description: Hardware allocation. Optional; `ivm` supplies defaults for anything omitted.

memory.description: RAM in GiB, written with a `G` suffix (e.g. `8G`); `ivm` converts to incus `GiB`.

disk.description: Root disk size in GiB, `G` suffix; `ivm` converts to incus `GiB`.

nested_virt.description: Run nested KVM inside this VM. Host-gated, NOT a per-VM incus setting: incus VMs already expose the host CPU (vmx/svm), so this works whenever the HOST kernel has nesting on (`kvm_intel nested=1` / `kvm_amd nested=1`). `ivm` only warns if the host looks disabled - it cannot change the host's modprobe config.

secureboot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Required true for Windows 11.

tpm.description: Attach a virtual TPM 2.0 device. Required for Windows 11.

os.description: Guest OS: the tier (linux/windows), the specific Linux distro, and where to fetch the disk image.

type.description: OS tier. `linux` = the unix provisioning path (distro_packages/dotfiles/post_install_script via incus exec); requires `distro`. `windows` = a SEPARATE tier (unattend / cloudbase-init); no `distro`, and the unix provisioning fields do not apply.

distro.description: Specific Linux distro (linux only). `ivm` derives BOTH the package manager (apt/zypper/dnf) and the ansible_os_family (Debian/Suse/RedHat) from it. `distro_package_groups` are resolved against ansible_os_family (so debian and ubuntu currently share the Debian package set). ansible_os_family is DERIVED, never specified by the user.

source.description: Where the disk image comes from.

uri.description: Image reference for the source (e.g. `debian/13` for the incus remote, or a file path for `iso`).

gui.description: Mark this a GUI/desktop VM. `ivm` then installs `spice-vdagent` (host<->guest clipboard + dynamic resolution via `ivm gui`'s SPICE console) and `xdg-user-dirs` (so the GTK file picker + apps resolve ~/Downloads etc.). The desktop itself (X11 vs Wayland, WM/DE) is whatever you install via packages. CONVENTION: `ivm` installs `spice-vdagent` but does NOT autostart it - on a bare WM (icewm) launch `spice-vdagent &` from the WM startup in `post_install_script` (same as fcitx5); DEs honoring XDG autostart (KDE/GNOME/LXQt) start it themselves. Without it the clipboard won't sync.

input_method.description: In-guest input method framework. `fcitx5` -> `ivm` writes the IM env vars to `/etc/environment` (`GTK_IM_MODULE`/`QT_IM_MODULE`/`XMODIFIERS`, which apply on both X11 and Wayland). Install the IME packages separately via `distro_package_groups: [cjk_input]`; autostart fcitx5 in `post_install_script` for a bare WM (icewm), DEs honoring XDG autostart (KDE/GNOME/LXQt) start it themselves.

timezone.description: Guest timezone. `host` = match the host's timezone.

tmpfs.description: Guest paths to back with tmpfs (RAM). DISCOURAGED in a VM: incus VMs have no balloon free-page-reporting, so tmpfs pages stay resident in the host QEMU process and are NOT returned to the host until the VM STOPS; and tmpfs only shrinks (to swap) if the guest HAS swap - the images usually don't, so without swap it is unreclaimable used RAM. Prefer leaving /tmp on the VM disk: the page cache already gives RAM-speed for hot temp files, cold data goes to disk (not scarce swap), and the RAM is reclaimable. If you must use it, cap the size and give the guest swap.

ssh_server.description: Optional in-guest sshd, for EXTERNAL / IDE-remote access only. The launcher's own shell uses `incus exec`, which needs no ssh.

authorized_keys.description: Host public-key file paths to install into the guest's authorized_keys.

net.description: Network attachment. Optional; default is NAT via incus's managed bridge (zero host setup, unlike virt-manager).

mode.description: `nat` = incus managed bridge (incusbr0): DHCP/DNS/outbound-NAT, host<->VM works, LAN cannot reach the VM, ZERO host setup. `macvlan` = VM gets a LAN IP via the `parent` NIC, no host bridge needed, BUT host<->VM is blocked (macvlan kernel limit). `bridge` = VM on the LAN via an EXISTING host bridge (`parent`), host<->VM works - but you must create that host bridge yourself (nmcli/netplan) first.

parent.description: Host NIC (for `macvlan`) or existing host bridge name (for `bridge`). Unused for `nat`.

mounts.description: virtio-fs shares. Applied ONLY at VM creation; frozen once the VM exists.

host.description: Host path. Shell-expanded on the HOST at init, relative to the current dir: `$(pwd)`, `$HOME`, `~`, and relative paths (`./x`) are allowed; the expanded absolute path is what gets passed to incus.

guest.description: Path inside the VM. Dev/agent project mounts go under `/workspaces/` (devcontainer compatibility); for a GUI app, share host XDG dirs at the guest user's own location (e.g. `/home/user/Downloads`) so apps find them by default. A mount under `/home/user/` is fine - `/home/user` is chowned to `user` at provision.

shadow.description: Subpaths relative to `guest` to mask with an empty mount, so the guest cannot see the host's real ones. High-risk things to hide from an agent: `.git`, `.vscode`, `.env`, etc.

shell_default_dir_after_login.description: Initial working directory for `ivm shell` / `shell-user` / `shell-root`, passed as `incus exec --cwd`. ONLY sets where the interactive shell starts: `$HOME` and a bare `cd` are unchanged. Typically a mounted project path; shell-expanded on the HOST at init like a mount's `guest` value, so `/workspaces/$(basename "$(pwd)")` resolves to the same dir as the mount it points into. Stored on the VM as `user.ivm_shell_default_dir_after_login` (change later with `ivm set guest-shell-dir`); if the dir is absent in the guest (e.g. a mount failed), `ivm shell` warns and starts in the default cwd. Optional; omit to start in incus's default (the home dir). Linux only.

distro_package_groups.description: Named package bundles defined in `roles/provision_distro_packages/defaults/main.yml` (variable `provision_distro_packages_<name>`), referenced here by the short `<name>`. Resolved against this VM's ansible_os_family (derived from `os.distro`): the bundle's `__common__` list plus its per-family overlay. (Linux only.)

distro_packages.description: Extra packages, literal names for THIS VM's distro. Flat (no per-distro dict) because `os` already pins one distro - so version-pinned names like `python3.13` go here.

thirdparty_software.description: Named non-distro install recipes defined in `roles/provision_thirdparty_software/defaults/main.yml` (variable `provision_thirdparty_software_<name>`), referenced by the short `<name>`. Each runs a shell snippet as ROOT in the guest (with an optional `already_installed` probe that skips it if present): 3rd-party repos (vscode), `curl|bash` installers (agent_claude), npm/pip globals (agent_codex). Resolved per ansible_os_family - the family's entry if defined, else `__common__` (OVERRIDE, not additive). A recipe's registry-declared `distro_packages` deps install via the package manager before any recipe runs - do NOT re-list them under this template's `distro_packages`. (Linux only.)

dotfiles.description: Which dotfile sets to stage host-side (via each role's deploy-*-config task) and push into the VM. Config only; the program itself (e.g. emacs) must still be listed in `distro_packages`.

post_install_script.description: Shell run as ROOT inside the VM after packages install (provisioning is a root task); shown in the init preview before it runs. To act as the unprivileged user (e.g. installers that target the user's home, like claude), drop with `runuser -l user -c '...'` / `su - user -c '...'` - root switches to anyone, no password. Provision-time only (host-operator-driven via incus exec); the runtime model where `user` has no sudo is unaffected. Linux only.

windows.description: Windows-only provisioning (used when os.type=windows). The unix provisioning fields (distro_packages, distro_package_groups, thirdparty_software, dotfiles, post_install_script) do NOT apply to Windows.

unattend.description: Path to a Windows answer file (unattend.xml) for unattended OOBE - automates account creation, locale, network, etc. Expanded host-side; attached at install.

post_install_powershell.description: PowerShell run in the guest after first boot (the Windows analog of post_install_script), e.g. `winget install ...`. Delivered via cloudbase-init / a scheduled FirstLogon command.

allOf.comment: Two tiers. windows: no unix provisioning fields, no os.distro; the `windows` block carries provisioning. linux: os.distro required, no `windows` block.
